headline: The US Army has ordered a new command to lead its move into drones and other autonomous weapons, following the Pentagon's plan for a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: a large military reorganisation around autonomous weapons, confirmed by an Army memo, though leadership, base and start date are not set.
importance_line: Soldiers, whose units are to gain drone and robotics specialists, and the Pentagon's weapons buyers are affected first, but the Army says specifics on structure, command and mission will come later, and the Pentagon's four-star command still needs an act of Congress, with a goal of 1 Oct 2027.
summary: Military Times reports that an Army memo dated 1 Oct 2026 and signed by Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle orders the creation of the Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM) and a single office to buy the Army's priority autonomous systems, following the 30 Sep 2026 announcement by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, head of the Pentagon, of a planned four-star Autonomous Warfare Command. The memo sets a fiscal 2028 deadline for buying and fielding autonomous systems such as artillery, combat vehicles, breaching systems and drones or robots working alongside crewed vehicles, but it leaves FASCOM's leader, base and start date open.
notes: Read in full from the pool fulltext. Robot-war story (counts toward the robot war limit). Memo dated 1 Oct 2026, reported 13 Oct 2026 with the Army's release, so NEW. The Army gave no answer on how FASCOM fits with T2COM and AutoWarCom or on cost.
